record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?

evidence.quote: Tiny defects look like points in M, so fields Φ(ξ) when restricted to the small ξ in Q will give ordinary local quantum fields on M. Will these form new local qfts in 2n-dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth oriented conformal manifold of even dimension 2n, and let Q = Q(M) denote its associated quasi Riemann surface, i.e. the space of integral (n-1)-currents (or, more generally, a suitable completion thereof) in M, equipped with the structure that generalizes the classical Riemann-surface picture for n = 1. Suppose one has a quantum field theory on Q whose fundamental fields Φ(ξ) are indexed by points ξ ∈ Q, generalizing the assignment of fields to points on a Riemann surface.

Consider the restriction of Φ(ξ) to "tiny" defects ξ ∈ Q—configurations that are, from the point of view of M, supported in arbitrarily small neighborhoods of single points of M, so that in the limit they behave as ordinary point insertions in M. The restricted operators then define local fields on the 2n-dimensional manifold M, and via their correlation functions produce a candidate local quantum field theory on M.

Question: Do such restricted fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories on a 2n-dimensional manifold M (for n ≥ 2)—that is, theories not equivalent to any previously known local QFT in 2n dimensions—and, more strongly, can one exhibit constructive examples and characterize the class of 2n-dimensional local QFTs that arise in this way?
artifact.category_tag: quasi Riemann surfaces and defect QFT
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of quasi Riemann surfaces and the conjecture that fields restricted to pointlike defects produce new 2n-dimensional local QFTs are explicitly posed as speculative open questions in the program on quasi Riemann surfaces. No published construction or proof addressing whether genuinely new 2n-dimensional local QFTs arise this way has been located; the topic remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces II. Questions, comments, speculations
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-Riemann surfaces are conformal 2n-manifolds; fields generalize from points on a Riemann surface to integral currents; the document is framed as questions and speculations.
status_evidence.claim: The framework is presented as open speculation rather than a body of established results, supporting the open status of the question.

status_evidence.title: QFT with defects in nLab
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of defect QFT; no construction of new 2n-dimensional local QFTs from pointlike-restricted quasi Riemann surface fields is reported.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on defect QFT do not record a resolution of this specific question.
